Flash Q. The name Z of this legendary estate originates from Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s 1816 poem Kubla Khan, where it is described as a "stately pleasure-dome." In the world of cinema in the movie X, it serves as the sprawling, unfinished mausoleum of a media tycoon, housing a private zoo, a mountain, and enough plundered European art to fill ten museums.
Decades later, a modern mogul Y paid homage to this fictional monument of ego by naming his 66,000-square-foot Washington residence "Z 2.0." Much like its cinematic predecessor, this real-life version is a marvel of its time, featuring high-tech "pins" that adjust the temperature and lighting to a guest's preference as they move through the rooms.
